h1:
Play La Ploen Buriram
Flower Gardens and a Learning Park for a Full Day Out
intro: Play La Ploen is a flower park and learning center spread across more than 400 rai in Buriram province. The draw is a cluster of themed greenhouses that coax cool-climate plants like tulips and lavender into bloom right in the middle of Isan, plus animal farms, a cactus garden, cafes, and on-site lodging. Kids and families can wander and take photos for hours. It is a relaxed kind of day out, a real change of pace from the Khmer temples and the football stadium in town.

blocks.html: If your Buriram trip is packed with Khmer temples and the football stadium and you want an easy day to break things up, Play La Ploen is the kind of place families love. It is a large flower park built as a learning center, with air-conditioned flower greenhouses, an animal farm where kids can feed the animals, a cactus garden, and a cafe to rest at in the middle of the grounds. You really can stroll and shoot photos at a leisurely pace, just like the name suggests.

Let's be straight about the location first. A lot of people assume Play La Ploen is near Nang Rong or close to Phanom Rung in the south of the province, but it's actually in Khu Mueang district, north of Buriram town, about 30 km out, roughly half an hour by car. If you plan to pair it with the cluster of temples to the south, leave plenty of travel time, because they're in opposite directions.

blocks.text: What kind of place is Play La Ploen

blocks.html: Play La Ploen positions itself as a tourism-focused learning center more than a theme park. The heart of it is a group of flower greenhouses, each on a different theme, planting blooms that rotate with the seasons. Around them you'll find animal farms, a model rice paddy, a small dinosaur garden, an antiques museum, and a health spa zone, all connected on foot within a single area. It suits anyone who wants to take their time.

items: Over 400 rai — it's a flower park, a learning center, lodging, and a seminar venue all in one.
Multiple themed greenhouses — cool-climate plants like tulips and lavender are grown to bloom in Isan.
Animal farms — sheep, horses, and small animals for kids to see up close and feed.
Cafe, restaurant, and souvenirs — eat, drink, and shop all in one spot, no need to head outside.
On-site lodging — a flower-garden-themed resort for anyone who wants an easy overnight stay.

items.label: Day trips from Buriram
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.html: The star of Play La Ploen is the air-conditioned flower greenhouses, which is how cool-climate plants that normally wouldn't grow in Isan can thrive here. Each greenhouse has its own theme and swaps out flower varieties through the year, so every visit looks a little different. Popular flowers to shoot include tulips in all colors, lavender, lilies, and roses.

items.name: Cool-climate flower greenhouse
items.blurb: The heart of the place, with tulips, lavender, and lilies in an air-conditioned room. The flowers change in cycles, and late in the year through early the next is peak season for colorful tulips. Great photos, and you stay cool.

items.name: Cactus garden
items.blurb: A zone of hundreds of cacti and succulents arranged in a desert style, with decorated corners for fun photos. Good for anyone who likes this kind of plant.

items.name: Fern and dinosaur zone
items.blurb: Set up as a prehistoric fern forest with small dinosaur figures tucked among the plants. Kids love it, and it's a fun walk that feels like stepping into another era.

blocks.title: When are the flowers at their best
blocks.html: Cool-climate flowers like tulips and lavender are usually at full bloom from late rainy season into the cool season, roughly November through February, when the flowers are dense and the weather is just right. If you come off-season, some greenhouses may be between planting cycles and the blooms will be thinner. It's worth calling or checking their Facebook page before you go, so you know which greenhouses are flowering at the time.

blocks.text: Animal farm and activities for kids

blocks.html: Beyond the flowers, Play La Ploen has an animal farm that kids especially love, with a sheep farm, a horse farm, and small animals you can get close to. At some spots you can buy feed for them. Add the model rice paddy and the nature-learning corners, and parents can keep kids walking around all day without them getting bored.

items: Sheep and horse farms — see them up close and feed them at some spots; little kids love it.
Model rice paddy and insect house — hands-on nature-learning corners, not just walking and looking.
Small dinosaur garden — dinosaur figures in a fern forest, cute for photos with the kids.
Photo spots throughout the garden — flower setups and decorations dotted around, easy to keep shooting as you walk.

blocks.html: Once you've worn yourself out walking the garden, you don't have to go looking for food outside, because Play La Ploen has a garden cafe to sit and sip coffee, plus a restaurant and a souvenir zone. If you want an easy overnight, there's an on-site resort decorated on a flower-garden theme, so you can get up early and stroll the garden before the crowds arrive.

items.name: Garden cafe
items.blurb: Sip coffee and other drinks among the plants and flowers. It's a good place to rest your legs between greenhouses, and the atmosphere is cool and easy.

items.name: Restaurant and souvenirs
items.blurb: There's a restaurant on the grounds for a proper meal, plus a souvenir zone with local products you can take home without stopping anywhere else.

items.name: On-site resort
items.blurb: Lodging decorated on a flower-garden theme for anyone who wants to stay over. Good for families who want to take it slow and stroll the garden first thing in the morning.

blocks.text: Entry fee, opening hours, and getting there

items: Entry fee — adults around 150 THB, children about 80 THB; seniors sometimes enter free (check the latest before you go).
Opening hours — open daily, roughly 08:00–17:00 (some sources list a 09:00 start, so check first).
Location — Khu Mueang district, north of Buriram town, about 30 km away, roughly half an hour by car.
Getting there — easiest by private car or rental; direct public transport is limited.
Time needed — allow half a day to a full day if you're coming with kids, since the grounds are big with several zones.

blocks.title: Check ahead to be sure
blocks.html: Entry fees and opening hours at places like this can shift with the season and special events. During flower festivals there may be special sessions or different pricing than usual. Before you go, call or message Play La Ploen directly on LINE for the most current details, especially if you're set on seeing a specific flower.

blocks.text: A full-day plan for Play La Ploen

blocks.html: Play La Ploen is an easy place to visit, no need to rush, because everything is in one area and within walking distance. Here's a day's rhythm that actually flows: start with the greenhouses in the morning before it gets hot, then move on to the animal farm and cafe later in the day.

Set off back to Buriram town.

items.note: Good for families who want an unhurried trip

blocks.text: Honest tips before you go to Play La Ploen

items: The cool season is the best value — around November to February, when the flowers are dense and the weather is cooler.
Check the flower cycle first — off-season, some greenhouses are between planting rounds; call or message on LINE to be sure.
Allow travel time — it's in Khu Mueang to the north, the opposite direction from Phanom Rung, so don't plan a tight back-to-back.
Coming with kids, budget the whole day — flowers, animal farm, cafe, and lots of space mean kids can keep busy for a long time.
Pack a hat and water — the greenhouses are cool and comfortable, but the open-air paths between zones get strong midday sun.

faq.q: Which district is Play La Ploen in, and how far is it from Buriram town?
faq.a: Play La Ploen is in Khu Mueang district, north of Buriram town, about 30 km away, roughly half an hour by car. It's not near Nang Rong or Phanom Rung to the south, as many people assume. If you want to pair it with the temple cluster, allow extra travel time since they're in opposite directions.

faq.q: How much is the entry fee for Play La Ploen, and what time does it open?
faq.a: Entry is around 150 THB for adults and about 80 THB for children. It's open daily, roughly 08:00–17:00 (some sources list a 09:00 start). During flower festivals there may be special sessions or pricing, so it's best to call or message on LINE to check before you go.

faq.q: When are the flowers most beautiful at Play La Ploen?
faq.a: From late rainy season into the cool season, roughly November through February, is peak for cool-climate flowers like tulips and lavender, with dense blooms and pleasant weather. If you come off-season, some greenhouses may be between planting cycles, so check which ones are flowering at the time.

faq.q: Is Play La Ploen good for taking kids?
faq.a: Very much so. Besides the flower gardens, there's a sheep farm, a horse farm, small animals to feed, a model rice paddy, and a small dinosaur garden. Kids can roam all day, the grounds are spacious, and there's an on-site cafe and restaurant to rest at conveniently.

faq.q: Does Play La Ploen have lodging, and do you need to stay over?
faq.a: There's an on-site resort decorated on a flower-garden theme. If you want an unhurried trip, you can stay over and stroll the garden in the morning before the crowds. But a day trip is plenty, since you can cover every zone in half a day to a full day.
